newsitem.title: USA: U.S. court denies tobacco class-action.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court denies tobacco class-action.

text.p: A federal court refused to certify a class-action lawsuit against the tobacco industry brought on behalf of Pennsylvania residents alleging they are addicted to cigarettes, Brown & Williamson said on Wednesday.

The ruling was the first denial of class certification of a case filed by plaintiffs lawyers after the big Castano case was decertified last year by a federal appeals court in New Orleans. Brown & Williamson is a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc.

In the Castano case, the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals rejected the class action, saying the differences in state laws and in the facts of individual cases were too great for class treatment on a nationwide basis.
After that ruling, the group of some 60 plaintiffs lawyers involved in the Castano case began filing separate suits in individual states, including the one filed in Pennsylvania.

Brown & Williamson, which is based in Louisville, said that in the Pennsylvania case, Arch vs. The American Tobacco Co., Judge Clarence Newcomber said a class action the size and magnitude envisioned by the plaintiffs could not be tried.

"The reality of this litigation is that there are simply too many individual issues and class members to try this case efficiently. The manageability problems which would be encountered in litigating and trying this case are staggering," Newcomer wrote.
